# 0001 Optional shout flag for greet

## Problem

`greet(name)` in `src/greet.js` always returns `Hello, ${name}!`. Callers that want a shouted greeting have to uppercase the string themselves, and nothing in the module offers that.

## Scope

In: an optional `shout` flag on `greet` that returns the same greeting in upper case, plus a node:test file that locks the default and the flag.

Out: other greeting text, name validation, locale-specific casing (for example Turkish i), a CLI, and any change to callers that omit the flag.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-01: `greet(name)` and `greet(name, { shout: false })` still return `Hello, ${name}!`
- [ ] AC-02: `greet(name, { shout: true })` returns that same greeting in upper case (`greet("Ada", { shout: true })` is `HELLO, ADA!`)

## Approach

`src/greet.js` gains an optional second argument, an options object `{ shout }`. Omitted options, `shout: false`, and any value other than boolean `true` leave the current template untouched. `shout: true` runs `String.prototype.toUpperCase()` on the finished greeting, so the name is uppercased too.

`src/greet.test.js` is new. `package.json` already runs `node --test` via `npm test`. No other file calls `greet`.

Rejected: a positional boolean (`greet(name, true)`). A named flag stays compatible when another option shows up, and it matches the request for a shout flag.

Risk: passing `null` as the second argument throws if the implementation destructures a default. Callers omit the argument or pass an object. Do not accept `null`.

## Open questions

- none

## Tasks

### T-01 Add the shout flag and its tests
- AC: AC-01, AC-02 | Files: src/greet.js, src/greet.test.js | Test: npm test -- src/greet.test.js
